newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban says Iran provocation continues.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban says Iran provocation continues.

text.p: Afghanistan's new Sunni Moslem rulers said on Friday that neighbouring Shi'ite Iran continued to provoke the Taleban government despite recent assurances that relations would improve.

Acting deputy foreign minister Sher Mohammad Stanakzai told reporters he had been assured during a meeting with Tehran's charge d'affaires on Tuesday that Iran wanted good relations with its eastern neighbour.

"He promised so many things: that border problems would be solved and would also try to normalise our relations but after a few days I see their religious leader declared against us, and their newspapers every day say something against us," he said.

Iran's spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has criticised the government in Kabul, which took power two weeks ago after a lightning offensive ousted the Iran-backed government of Burhanuddin Rabbani, calling it "un-Islamic".
Stanakzai said that while the Taleban wanted to solve its problems with Iran it would not allow Teheran to interfere in what he called its internal affairs.

"We will never allow Iranians to interfere in our affairs. There are many Sunnis in their countries and they are suffering badly from Shias, but we never called on them anything regarding those things, it is their own internal affairs.
"So we have told them also not to interfere in our internal affairs, clearly we have told them," he said.

The Taleban is facing military setbacks on its northern front as former military chief Ahmad Shah Masood, defending the Panjsher valley, has forged a defensive alliance with militia leaders Abdul Rashid Dostum and Shia leader Karim Khalili.
